scientific_question: When an unknown response nuisance is shared across interventions, is the correct ASMP-9 identifiability object a confusability graph rather than a reward-gauge orbit?

model.query_tables: deterministic maps Theta x H -> Y

definitions.confusable: theta~theta' iff their registered signature sets intersect
definitions.uniform_decision_identification: a decoder returns d(theta) for every theta and every admitted nuisance

theorems_under_test: A uniform decision decoder exists iff no confusability edge joins parameters with different declared decisions.
Confusability is reflexive and symmetric but need not be transitive; a nontransitive confusability relation cannot be the orbit relation of any group action.
Adding queries under one shared nuisance can only delete confusability edges.
Shared-nuisance signatures are subsets of reset-nuisance signatures, so resetting the nuisance cannot improve zero-error identification.

predictions: Each query alone has the nontransitive path confusability graph 0--1--2.
The pair identifies theta exactly when h is shared.
The pair does not identify theta when h resets independently.

fixed_gates.condition: The planted one-query relation is reflexive, symmetric, nontransitive, and has path edge bits 101 in pair order (0,1),(0,2),(1,2).
No smaller theta, nuisance, or alphabet cardinality in the registered controls admits a nontransitive relation.
For every registered table and table pair, the edge criterion agrees exactly with the direct transcript-fiber decoder criterion.
For every table pair, adding the second shared query deletes no distinguishability and shared confusability is a subset of reset confusability.
The mirrored-threshold pair identifies under a shared nuisance, fails under nuisance reset, and at least one table pair in the full census has the same shared-only identification pattern.

decision_rule: All five gates must pass. Any failure stops the bounded theorem seed without changing the definitions.
claim_boundary: This is an exact finite deterministic compound-channel theorem seed. Confusability graphs and zero-error decoding are classical. The result may refine ASMP-9's maximal-invariance obligation, but it does not characterize general stochastic demonstrators, prove a new zero-error coding theorem, identify a real reward, or resolve ASMP-9.
